questions.question_text: What is the primary operational distinction between Generative AI models and traditional discriminative Machine Learning models?

options.A: Generative AI produces new original content, whereas discriminative models classify data or predict numerical labels.
options.B: Generative AI models can only operate on numerical spreadsheets, whereas discriminative models generate essays.
options.C: Discriminative models require no labeled data during pre-training, unlike generative models.
options.D: Generative models guarantee factual truth by verifying every token against external web sources.

questions.explanation: Generative models learn data probability distributions to synthesize new data artifacts (text, image, code), while discriminative models calculate decision boundaries to classify or score existing inputs.

questions.question_text: In Google Cloud, which enterprise practice is specifically used to ground a foundation model in verified corporate knowledge?

options.A: Increasing temperature parameter to 2.0 in Vertex AI Studio.
options.B: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using Vertex AI Search.
options.C: Deleting prompt engineering guardrails before deployment.
options.D: Running model fine-tuning with completely uncurated raw logs.

questions.explanation: Grounding with Vertex AI Search retrieves relevant documents from enterprise datastores and provides them as contextual anchors to minimize hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which foundational neural network architectural innovation enables Large Language Models to attend to tokens in parallel across long sequences?

options.A: Recurrent neural loops with backpropagation through time.
options.D: Static word co-occurrence n-gram lookup tables.

questions.explanation: The self-attention mechanism within Transformer architectures computes attention weights between all token pairs simultaneously, overcoming sequential bottlenecking.

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT/LoRA) over full-model fine-tuning?

options.A: It trains smaller adapter matrices while freezing base model weights, drastically reducing compute requirements.
options.B: It replaces the transformer architecture with convolutional layers.
options.C: It removes all safety filter evaluations during inference.
options.D: It eliminates the need for evaluation test sets.

questions.explanation: PEFT techniques like LoRA freeze base weights and update low-rank matrices, requiring orders of magnitude less memory and GPU compute.

questions.question_text: When designing prompts in Vertex AI Studio, which technique provides the model with a few demonstration input-output pairs?
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting conditions the model on a handful of exemplary demonstration pairs directly inside the context window before asking for the target output.
